answer: Picture an agent market on a remote mesa where the only oasis is shared compute. To drink, each new agent must lock a bond that matures slowly, like a cedar adding rings, and an existing member must co-sign it. If the newcomer is caught colluding, both bonds are slashed. A sybil attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must freeze a thousand bonds for months and find honest sponsors willing to gamble their own stake, turning cheap identities into expensive, risky ones.
